categories.main_business_segments: Molina Healthcare operates four reportable segments: Medicaid, Medicare, Marketplace, and Other. The company is a pure-play government-sponsored healthcare business providing managed healthcare services primarily under Medicaid and Medicare programs, and through state insurance marketplaces. As of December 31, 2022, the company served approximately 5.3 million members across 19 states, with Medicaid representing 80% of consolidated premium revenue.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced data analytics, predictive analytics, and medical informatics to support care management and medical cost control. Core operational methods include capitated and fee-for-service payment arrangements with providers, utilization management based on evidence-based practices, population health management programs tailored to member needs, and pharmacy benefit management services outsourced to CVS Caremark. The company also employs centralized information technology infrastructure managed through a third-party vendor agreement for claims processing, enrollment systems, and data security.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are state Medicaid agencies and the federal government (CMS). The company serves low-income families and individuals eligible for Medicaid, Medicare beneficiaries (particularly dual-eligible individuals), and low-income individuals purchasing through state insurance marketplaces. End markets include Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Medicaid Aged/Blind/Disabled (ABD), Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), Medicaid Expansion, Long-Term Services and Supports (LTSS), Medicare Advantage, and ACA Marketplace plans.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates across 19 states with significant presence in California, New York, Texas, Washington, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan, South Carolina, and other states. Major state contracts include New York (12% of Medicaid premium revenue), Texas (15%), Washington (17%), and California (8%, expected to exceed 10% in 2024). The company recently expanded into Nevada, Iowa, Nebraska, and Mississippi through new Medicaid procurement awards.
categories.supply_chain_position: Molina Healthcare operates in the midstream of the healthcare supply chain as a managed care intermediary. The company contracts with upstream providers (physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, ancillary providers) and receives capitated payments from downstream government payers (state Medicaid agencies and CMS). The company arranges, pays for, and manages healthcare services, bearing financial risk for medical costs while receiving fixed per-member-per-month premium payments.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include organic growth through new state procurement opportunities and market share expansion, strong medical cost ratio (MCR) and general and administrative (G&A) expense management, inorganic growth through accretive acquisitions, and capital reinvestment or shareholder returns. The company is building future capabilities in complex care management, scalable technology infrastructure, advanced data analytics, and compliance operations. Recent focus areas include expansion in California, Iowa, Nebraska, and long-term services and supports through acquisitions.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through fixed per-member-per-month (PMPM) capitated premium payments from state Medicaid agencies and the federal government (CMS) for Medicare and Marketplace programs. Premium rates vary by state, program type, demographics, and health risk factors. Additional revenue includes premium tax revenue (pass-through taxes), investment income, and service revenue from long-term services and supports consultative services. In 2022, premium revenue of $30.9 billion represented 96.6% of total revenue of $32.0 billion.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In Medicaid, primary competitors include Centene Corporation, CVS Health Corporation, Elevance Health, Inc., and UnitedHealth Group Incorporated. In Medicare, major competitors are CVS Health Corp., Humana Inc., and UnitedHealth Group Inc. In Marketplace, the primary competitor is Centene Corporation. Molina competes on provider network quality, service quality, reputation, financial resources, and quality scores. The company is positioned as a pure-play government-sponsored healthcare provider with a focus on low-cost, high-quality care delivery.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Molina Healthcare is a FORTUNE 500 company (ranked 125) with 2022 total revenue of $32.0 billion, up 15% from $27.8 billion in 2021. Premium revenue grew 15% to $30.9 billion. Net income was $792 million ($13.55 per diluted share) in 2022, up from $659 million ($11.25 per diluted share) in 2021. The company has demonstrated consistent growth through acquisitions generating approximately $10 billion in annual premium revenue since 2020, and organic membership growth of 59,000 members year-over-year to 5.3 million total members.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Molina differentiates itself as a low-cost, high-quality, reliable health plan delivering government-sponsored care with strong member outcomes. Key value propositions include effective and appropriate access to care at the right time and setting, emphasis on preventive healthcare and primary care coordination, comprehensive care management programs addressing physical health and social determinants, reliable service and seamless member experience, and proven ability to manage medical costs while maintaining quality. The company emphasizes its singular focus on government-sponsored healthcare, enabling identification and implementation of operational efficiencies that competitors with broader portfolios may lack.
